name: Smilax

project_scope.selection_mode: Genus comparison lesson from durable Smilacaceae family roadmap
project_scope.admission_note: Both source-pool concepts are already reconciled as accepted names in the family module. This genus lesson does not install or promote species.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: At a leafy node, find the paired tendrils associated with the petiole, then hold the leaf to the light: several strong longitudinal/arcuate veins are connected by a visible net of smaller cross-veins.
shared_genus_characters.vegetative: Perennial rhizomatous climbing vines or shrubs, often prickly; leaves alternate, usually leathery, prominently 3-5-veined with reticulate cross-veins; tendrils arise from the petiole region.
shared_genus_characters.reproductive: Plants usually dioecious; small greenish flowers are grouped in umbels and have 6 tepals.
shared_genus_characters.fruit: Round berries, commonly black at maturity in the two project species, with 1-3 seeds.
shared_genus_characters.genus_confirmation: Prickly climbing vine + petiolar tendrils + broad 3-5-veined reticulate leaf + small 6-tepaled umbels + berries is the project Smilax package.

species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Thicker leaves; often lobed or hastate but highly variable; broad cartilaginous marginal band.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: Use several leaves plus the cartilaginous margin and stout flattened prickles; do not rely on lobing alone.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Leaf shape can vary dramatically on one plant.

species_comparison_matrix.look_first: Lower-stem bristles/prickles plus basal leaf margin
species_comparison_matrix.leaf: Thinner, mostly unlobed leaves; basal margins minutely serrulate.
species_comparison_matrix.stem_armature: Conspicuous unequal, flexible dark bristles/prickles on lower stems.
species_comparison_matrix.best_separator: Flexible unequal bristles plus basal serrulation are the strongest project tie-breakers.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: A single unlobed leaf is not enough; pair margin and stem-armature characters.

decision_sequence: Confirm Smilax first: petiolar tendrils + 3-5 strong veins with reticulate cross-veins.
Inspect multiple mature leaves rather than one leaf shape.
Thick leaf with broad cartilaginous margin, often lobed/hastate + stout flattened prickles → S. bona-nox door.
Thinner mostly unlobed leaf with basal minute serrulation + flexible unequal dark bristles on lower stems → S. tamnoides door.
If armature and leaf-margin characters disagree or are not visible, leave the species unresolved until reproductive/vegetative details can be photographed.
overlap_and_cautions: Both species can be prickly climbing vines with black berries; fruit color alone does not separate them.
S. bona-nox leaf shape is extremely variable, including variation on one plant.
Do not use 'lobed = bona-nox' as a one-character rule.
Tendrils and reticulate venation are genus-recognition characters, not species separators.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Smilax combines petiolar tendrils with a monocot 6-tepal flower plan and the characteristic strong-vein + cross-vein leaf architecture.
Confirm tendril origin, leaf venation and umbels rather than using prickles alone.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Teach the margin/texture distinction without overfitting to leaf outline.
Show why Smilax is a broad-leaved monocot that can fool learners.
Late-season genus confirmation; not a stand-alone species separator.

media_routing.joey_media: Saved Joey routing was already checked by the family module; no direct Smilacaceae target frame is currently indexed.
media_routing.instruction: Prefer real project/user/Texas material that clearly shows the exact margin and prickle characters; do not substitute generic greenbrier glamour shots for diagnostic macros.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: If a future source-pool Smilax has intermediate or conflicting prickle/margin characters, send the exact specimen/observation to Genus Diagnostic Review rather than forcing it into either species.
Species-level county nativity and installation remain outside this genus lesson lane.
